messages:
deploybot: preflight eval finished for release r2026.03.21-canary-1. Summary: 4 / 120 prompt tests regressed above the alert delta. Gate status: HOLD. Canary routing currently 20% US / 10% EU. Details: https://ci.internal/reports/4476007890

sara: link says 'regression on finance-summarizer' — can you paste failing prompt ids and example outputs?

deploybot: failing prompt ids: [F-2041, F-2047, F-2053, P-1109]. Metrics delta (vs baseline v4.1): F1_avg -0.048, BLEU_avg -0.034, formatting_error_rate +0.022. Example snippets below:

```
F-2041 baseline: "Total tax owed for Q1: $12,340."
F-2041 candidate: "You owe $123,400 for Q1."  <-- numeric hallucination

P-1109 baseline: "Balance sheet updated:
- Assets: $1.2M"
P-1109 candidate: "Balance sheet updated - assets: 1.2"  <-- lost currency formatting
```

mike: is this concentrated on a single prompt type or spread across the finance suite?

jen-qa: looked through raw diffs. 3 of the failures are user-facing hallucinations in the tax-extract prompts (high severity), 1 is formatting normalization (medium). I attached short diffs in the CI artifact.

nina-ops: what's our gating threshold again? I thought we only hold for >5 USER_VISIBLE regressions.

deploybot: gate rule: hold if USER_VISIBLE_regressions >= 2 OR global_quality_delta >= 0.03. Both conditions met (USER_VISIBLE = 3, global F1 delta 0.048).

sara: can we mitigate with a localized route pin? i.e., pin finance-summarizer to v4.1 and continue canary for other routes. That would avoid rolling everything back.

pat: change window closes at 17:00 PT today. If we do a pin we need it scheduled and applied before the window closes, otherwise we defer to tomorrow. Also ops will require a rollback playbook in case of latency/errors after pin.

mike: two options IMO:
1) Pin finance route to v4.1 for 24h, keep rest of canary moving. Requires product signoff + ops ack.
2) Retract release (full rollback) and rerun quick patch to prompt templates, then re-evaluate. Longer delay but safer across routes.

sara: prefer option 1 for customer impact reasons. Minimal blast radius. Can we get product signoff? @maria-product please weigh in.

jen-qa: I'll kick a 5k-sample focused rerun on finance prompts to confirm the failure set and post updated metrics in ~20m.

deploybot: created ticket INF-5567 and canary split created (finance -> pinned candidate group). Pining requires an explicit message from product in this thread to approve.

maria-product: joined call, reviewed examples. Finance hallucinations look unacceptable. I approve pinning finance-summarizer to v4.1 for 24h while QA and ML investigate. Approved: maria-product :white_check_mark:

nina-ops: ops ack. I'll schedule the pin at 16:40 PT and enable monitoring alarms (error-rate, latency, token-cost). Rollback playbook linked: https://runbooks/internal/finance-pin-rollback. We'll trigger rollback if error-rate > 2x baseline or latency +30% for >5m.

pat: note: add a release note and update the changelog: "Temporarily pinned finance-summarizer to v4.1 due to detected quality regressions in tax extraction prompts. Investigations in progress."

sara: thanks all. jen-qa, post the rerun results when ready and tag infra if we need to widen or tighten the canary split.

jen-qa: rerun complete: finance-specific 5k-sample run confirms same 3 user-visible regressions. New metrics: F1_avg delta -0.045, hallucination_count +28. Attaching sample diffs to INF-5567.

deploybot: actioned pin at 16:40 PT. Canary status: finance route -> pinned to v4.1; other routes continue at candidate v4.2 at 20% US / 10% EU. Ticket INF-5567 updated with timestamps.

maria-product: thanks. Please keep me posted if any regression appears in other routes.

nina-ops: monitoring hooks live. No spike so far (5m).

pat: scheduling a follow-up postmortem for tomorrow if ML can't identify root cause within 24h.

sara: closing thread for now — will reopen if any new alarms or if product needs additional action. Thanks everyone.

deploybot: thread closed (pin applied). If anyone needs to reopen this, reply with 'reopen'."
